claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003.

claims.claim: CHE-1 specifies the identity of ASE neurons by activating expression of ASE-specific genes.
claims.source: To assay restriction, we have used the overexpression of terminal selector CHE-1, a Zn-finger TF, which is normally only expressed in two glutamatergic ASE sensory neurons and which specifies the identity of these neurons by activating expression of ASE-specific genes (Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2007; Patel et al., 2012; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013; Uchida et al., 2003.

claims.claim: unc-3 is a COE (Collier/Olf1/Ebf) TF which specifies the identity of cholinergic motor neurons.
claims.source: To understand the mechanistic basis of the plasticity-restricting function of terminal selectors, we focused on unc-3, a COE (Collier/Olf1/Ebf) TF which specifies the identity of cholinergic motor neurons (MNs).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the context and citations in the manuscript (Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998).

claims.claim: When CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages (<300 min), gcy-5prom::gfp is broadly activated in numerous cells.
claims.source: When CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages (<300 min), gcy-5prom::gfp is broadly activated in numerous cells (Figure 1Aiii).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aiii.

claims.claim: Induction of CHE-1hs during larval development results in an increasingly restricted activation of gcy-5.
claims.source: Induction of CHE-1hs during larval development results in an increasingly restricted activation of gcy-5, and the animals retain a normal overall morphology (Figure 1Aiv–viii).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aiv-viii.

claims.claim: Cells that express gcy-5 in response to larval CHE-1hs are those that have just been generated and hence are still differentiating.
claims.source: With the exception of a few neurons in the head and tail, cells that express gcy-5 in response to larval CHE-1hs are those that have just been generated and hence are still differentiating (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: CHE-1hs induction in the L2/L3 stage activates gcy-5 in seam cells and ventral nerve cord (VNC) neurons, which are dividing and differentiating at this time.
claims.source: For instance, CHE-1hs induction in the L2/L3 stage activates gcy-5 in seam cells and ventral nerve cord (VNC) neurons, which are dividing and differentiating at this time.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and observations in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Activation of gcy-5fosmid::gfp after L2 CHE-1hs expression is enriched in rab-3low cells.
claims.source: In these worms, activation of gcy-5fosmid::gfp after L2 CHE-1hs expression is enriched in rab-3low cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A), showing that cells that are dividing and differentiating are more receptive to CHE-1 than cells that have already differentiated.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Vulval muscle cells, which are dividing and differentiating at the L3 stage, are receptive to CHE-1hs at this stage.
claims.source: We also observe that vulval muscle cells, which are dividing and differentiating at the L3 stage are receptive to CHE-1hs at this stage (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: At the L4 and adult stages, when all tissues have differentiated, the only cells that activate gcy-5prom::gfp in response to CHE-1hs are a handful of neurons and pharyngeal muscle cells.
claims.source: At the L4 and adult stages, when all tissues have differentiated, the only cells that activate gcy-5prom::gfp in response to CHE-1hs are a handful of neurons and pharyngeal muscle cells, suggesting that these differentiated cells provide some molecular context which makes them amenable to che-1 activity (Figure 1Aviii and B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Aviii and B.

claims.claim: The CHE-1 responsive neurons include the RIS, CEP, ASK, and ASI neurons.
claims.source: The CHE-1 responsive neurons include the RIS, CEP, ASK, and ASI neurons.
claims.evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claims.claim: Expression of gcy-5prom::gfp overlaps with the expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA, indicating that the endogenous gcy-5 gene is induced by ectopic CHE-1hs.
claims.source: Additionally, gcy-5 smFISH of these worms shows that expression of gcy-5prom::gfp overlaps with the expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA, indicating that the endogenous gcy-5 gene is induced by ectopic CHE-1hs and that the transgene gcy-5prom::gfp reliably replicates the activity of the endogenous gcy-5 locus (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: After heatshock induction in adults, both che-1 mRNA and protein can be detected in all cell types.
claims.source: Ater heatshock induction in adults, both che-1 mRNA and protein can be detected in all cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C,D.

claims.claim: A synthetic strong reporter that contains a 4X multimerized CHE-1 binding site is expressed broadly, in all somatic cell types at every stage of development, in response to CHE-1hs expression.
claims.source: We find that this gcy-54XASE::gfp reporter is expressed broadly, in all somatic cell types at every stage of development, in response to CHE-1hs expression from both the multi-copy and single-copy heatshock-inducible transgenes (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: If CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages, the resulting arrested embryos and larvae activate broad expression of gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp.
claims.source: If CHE-1hs is induced during early embryonic stages, the resulting arrested embryos and larvae activate broad expression of gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Expression of gcy-6 and gcy-7 markers becomes more restricted as CHE-1hs is induced at later stages.
claims.source: Expression of these markers also becomes more restricted as CHE-1hs is induced at later stages.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: Ectopic induction of gcy-6 and gcy-7 is not as broad as gcy-5 and no ectopic expression is detected when CHE-1hs is induced in larval stages.
claims.source: However, ectopic induction of these genes is not as broad as gcy-5 and no ectopic expression is detected when CHE-1hs is induced in larval stages. (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: CHE-1 is sufficient to activate ASER-specific genes, but may require other co-activators to activate ASEL-specific genes.
claims.source: Previous analysis has shown that while CHE-1 is sufficient to activate ASER-specific genes, it may require other co-activators to activate ASEL-specific genes (Etchberger et al., 2009; Hobert, 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Etchberger et al., 2009; Hobert, 2014.

claims.claim: CHE-1 driven by all neuronal promoters resulted in broad ectopic expression of gcy-5prom::gfp, gcy-5fosmid::gfp, and ceh-36fosmid::yfp.
claims.source: CHE-1 driven by all neuronal promoters resulted in broad ectopic expression of gcy-5prom::gfp, gcy-5fosmid::gfp, and ceh-36fosmid::yfp (another che-1 target, a homeodomain TF expressed in ASEL/R and AWC neurons) .
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp show restricted activation in only 1–2 extra cells when CHE-1 is driven by neuronal promoters.
claims.source: However, gcy-6fosmid::gfp and gcy-7prom::rfp show restricted activation in only 1–2 extra cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: Transgenic animals expressing CHE-1 in the hypodermis or muscle showed gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the respective tissues.
claims.source: Transgenic animals expressing CHE-1 in the hypodermis or muscle also showed gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the respective tissues (Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3b,c.

claims.claim: A wide range of cell types are receptive to CHE-1 activity after post-mitotic division while they are terminally differentiating.
claims.source: In combination with the heatshock experiments, these experiments show that a wide range of cell types are receptive to CHE-1 activity after post-mitotic division while they are terminally differentiating.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1 and related supplements.

claims.claim: Once terminal differentiation is accomplished, most cells lose their multipotency and become refractory to CHE-1 activity.
claims.source: Once terminal differentiation is accomplished, most cells lose their multipotency and become refractory to CHE-1 activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claims.claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs are born and found in approximately their wildtype positions in the ventral nerve cord (VNC), retro-vesicular ganglion (RVG), and pre-anal ganglion (PAG) of the worm.
claims.source: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs are born and found in approximately their wildtype positions in the ventral nerve cord (VNC), retro-vesicular ganglion (RVG), and pre-anal ganglion (PAG) of the worm.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claims.claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs express pan-neuronal identity markers, and form axonal projections.
claims.source: They express pan-neuronal identity markers, and form axonal projections.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claims.claim: unc-3(-) cholinergic MNs lack expression of all the acetylcholine pathway genes, numerous other terminal identity genes, show defects in synaptogenesis and are non-functional.
claims.source: However, these neurons lack expression of all the acetylcholine pathway genes, numerous other terminal identity genes, show defects in synaptogenesis and are non-functional (Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kratsios et al., 2011; Prasad et al., 1998.

claims.claim: In wildtype worms, an average of 11 neurons activate gcy-5prom::gfp at the L2 stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression, and this number is reduced to an average of 2 neurons by the L4 and adult stages.
claims.source: In wildtype worms, we find that an average of 11 neurons activate gcy-5prom::gfp at the L2 stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression, and this number is reduced to an average of 2 neurons by the L4 and adult stages.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: In unc-3 mutants, a significantly higher number of neurons express gcy-5prom::gfp at every developmental stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression.
claims.source: In unc-3 mutants, a significantly higher number of neurons express gcy-5prom::gfp at every developmental stage upon ectopic CHE-1hs expression (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the VNC was not seen when unc-3 mutants were heatshocked in the absence of the hsprom::che-1 transgene.
claims.source: gcy-5prom::gfp expression in the VNC was not seen when unc-3 mutants were heatshocked in the absence of the hsprom::che-1 transgene, showing that the loss of unc-3 is not sufficient for an identity switch.
claims.evidence: This is a control experiment demonstrating that unc-3 loss alone does not activate gcy-5.

claims.claim: Expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA was induced in unc-3(-) cells to a similar extent as the gcy-5prom::gfp reporter.
claims.source: Additionally, smFISH of these worms showed that expression of endogenous gcy-5 mRNA was also induced in unc-3(-) cells to a similar extent (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: About 30% of affected neurons in unc-3 mutants express gcy-5 in response to CHE-1hs induction.
claims.source: On average, about 30% of affected neurons in unc-3 mutants express gcy-5 in response to CHE-1hs induction.
claims.evidence: This is a quantification of the experimental data.

claims.claim: Genes that showed increased induction after L4 CHE-1hs in unc-3 included the glutamate transporter eat-4fosmid::yfp, the homeodomain TF ceh-36fosmid::yfp, and the ciliary protein ift-20prom::rfp.
claims.source: Genes that showed increased induction after L4 CHE-1hs in unc-3 included the glutamate transporter eat-4fosmid::yfp, the homeodomain TF ceh-36fosmid::yfp, and the ciliary protein ift-20prom::rfp (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: No induction of gcy-6fosmid::gfp or gcy-7prom::rfp was observed in wildtype or unc-3(-) neurons.
claims.source: No induction of gcy-6fosmid::gfp or gcy-7prom::rfp was observed in wildtype or unc-3(-) neurons, which is consistent with the idea that che-1 is not sufficient for the induction of these genes, as discussed earlier (0 neurons induced in >20 worms checked).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: Neither unc-4 mutants, nor unc-55; mab-9 double mutants show increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in cholinergic MNs in response to CHE-1hs.
claims.source: Neither unc-4 mutants, nor unc-55; mab-9 double mutants, however, show increased induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in cholinergic MNs in response to CHE-1hs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: A disruption of function and identity-specific transcriptional programs does not automatically make cells more plastic.
claims.source: These data demonstrate that a disruption of function and identity-specific transcriptional programs does not automatically make cells more plastic.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the unc-4 and unc-55; mab-9 mutant data.

claims.claim: 30% of ets-5(-) BAG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp in response to adult CHE-1hs as opposed to 4% of wildtype BAG neurons.
claims.source: Specifically, ets-5 is a terminal selector for the CO2 sensing BAG neurons (Guillermin et al., 2011). In our assay, 30% of ets-5(-) BAG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp in response to adult CHE-1hs as opposed to 4% of wildtype BAG neurons (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Guillermin et al., 2011.

claims.claim: 23% of ttx-1(-) AFD neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp after adult CHE-1hs whereas 2% of wildtype AFD neurons do.
claims.source: ttx-1 is a terminal selector for thermosensory AFD neurons (Satterlee et al., 2001; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013) and 23% of ttx-1(-) AFD neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp after adult CHE-1hs whereas 2% of wildtype AFD neurons do (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and citations to Satterlee et al., 2001; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Removing both ttx-1 and ceh-14 results in 34.3% of AFD neurons expressing gcy-5fosmid::gfp compared to 4.8% in matched wildtypes.
claims.source: Removing both ttx-1 and ceh-14, the co-factor of ttx-1 in AFD specification, results in a 34.3% phenotype compared to 4.8% in matched wildtypes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data.

claims.claim: An average increase of five gcy-5fosmid-positive neurons is found in the tails of ceh-14 mutants upon CHE-1 induction.
claims.source: ceh-14 also acts as a terminal selector in several distinct tail neuron classes (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). We found an average increase of five gcy-5fosmid-positive neurons in the tails of ceh-14 mutants upon CHE-1 induction (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claims.claim: 30% of lin-11(-) ASG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp as opposed to 2% of wildtype ASG neurons.
claims.source: Lastly, lin-11 is required for terminal identity specification of ASG neurons (Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013), and 30% of lin-11(-) ASG neurons express gcy-5fosmid::gfp as opposed to 2% of wildtype ASG neurons (Figure 3d).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d and citation to Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claims.claim: No increases in induction of gcy-5prom::gfp or ceh-36fosmid::yfp were detected in response to CHE-1hs in the GABAergic MNs of unc-30.
claims.source: unc-30 is the terminal selector for GABAergic MNs in the VNC and unc-42 is the terminal selector for ASH sensory neurons (Baran et al., 1999; Cinar et al., 2005; Jin et al., 1994; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013). No increases in induction of gcy-5prom::gfp or ceh-36fosmid::yfp were detected in response to CHE-1hs in the GABAergic MNs of unc-30 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, data only shown for ceh-36fosmid::yfp).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and citations to Baran et al., 1999; Cinar et al., 2005; Jin et al., 1994; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Neither gcy-5fosmid::rfp, nor ceh-36fosmid::yfp was detected in the ASH neurons of unc-42 mutants after CHE-1 misexpression.
claims.source: In the case of unc-42 mutants, neither gcy-5fosmid::rfp, nor ceh-36fosmid::yfp was detected in the ASH neurons after CHE-1 misexpression (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, data only shown for gcy-5fosmid::rfp).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Expression of che-1 early in the development of GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons leads to activation of target genes.
claims.source: Expression of che-1 early in the development of GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons does lead to activation of target genes, based on tissue-specific promoter driven expression of che-1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Activation of CHE-1hs in L4s/adults results in the expression of gcy-54XASE::gfp in both GABAergic MNs and ASH neurons.
claims.source: Additionally, activation of CHE-1hs in L4s/adults results in the expression of gcy-54XASE::gfp in both sets of neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F.

claims.claim: While unc-30 and unc-42 are required for terminal differentiation, they are dispensable for restricting cellular plasticity.
claims.source: Therefore, we conclude that while unc-30 and unc-42 are required for terminal differentiation, they are dispensable for restricting cellular plasticity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on unc-30 and unc-42 mutants.

claims.claim: The loss of a terminal identity in itself is not sufficient to keep a neuron in a plastic state.
claims.source: The negative results with unc-30 and unc-42 demonstrate that the loss of a terminal identity in itself it not sufficient to keep a neuron in a plastic state.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on unc-30 and unc-42 mutants.

claims.claim: The restriction of plasticity is a distinct and parallel function carried out by certain terminal selector TFs.
claims.source: This suggests that the restriction of plasticity is a distinct and parallel function carried out by certain terminal selector TFs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential effects of various terminal selector mutants.

claims.claim: The unc-3::mNG::AID allele displays wildtype locomotion and expresses cholinergic MN markers at near wildtype levels in the absence of TIR1 and auxin.
claims.source: In the absence of TIR1 and auxin, the unc-3::mNG::AID worms display wildtype locomotion and express cholinergic MN markers at near wildtype levels (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: Cholinergic MNs of unc-3::mNG::AID worms were receptive to CHE-1hs, even in the absence of TIR1 and auxin.
claims.source: However, cholinergic MNs of these worms were receptive to CHE-1hs, even in the absence of TIR1 and auxin (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claims.claim: When CHE-1hs is overexpressed in adult worms containing unc-3::mNG::AID, expression of gcy-5prom::gfp is observed at a penetrance indistinguishable from that observed in the unc-3 null allele.
claims.source: When CHE-1hs is overexpressed in adult worms containing unc-3::mNG::AID, expression of gcy-5prom::gfp is observed at a penetrance indistinguishable from that observed in the unc-3 null allele.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: In the unc-3::mNG::AID allele, cholinergic MNs differentiate largely normally, and yet retain plasticity in response to CHE-1hs activity.
claims.source: Hence, in this allele the cholinergic MNs differentiate largely normally, and yet retain plasticity in response to CHE-1hs activity.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on the unc-3::mNG::AID allele.

claims.claim: Terminal selector TFs control restriction independently of specification.
claims.source: This allele therefore supports the hypothesis that terminal selector-like TFs control restriction independently of specification.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the unc-3::mNG::AID allele data.

claims.claim: The ace-2 LacO array is transcriptionally active in wildtype cholinergic neurons but not in unc-3 mutants.
claims.source: The ace-2 LacO array is transcriptionally active in wildtype cholinergic neurons but not in unc-3 mutants (Figure 5B,C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claims.claim: The ace-2 LacO array showed a significantly higher GFP pixel count in wildtype VNC neurons as compared to unc-3.
claims.source: Consistent with its expression, the ace-2 LacO array showed a significantly higher GFP pixel count in wildtype VNC neurons as compared to unc-3 (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claims.claim: The size of the GFP spot on the gcy-5 LacO array was increased in unc-3 mutant MNs compared to wildtype.
claims.source: We then quantified GFP spots on the LacO array that contains gcy-5, the ASE-specific CHE-1 target gene that is normally not expressed in VNC MNs. In this case, the size of the GFP spot was increased in unc-3 mutant MNs compared to wildtype (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: The gcy-5 locus is in a less compact state in unc-3 mutant cholinergic MNs, which may make it more amenable to activation by CHE-1.
claims.source: These data show that the gcy-5 locus is in a less compact state in unc-3 mutant cholinergic MNs, which may make it more amenable to activation by CHE-1.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LacO/LacI spot assay data.

claims.claim: The size of the gcy-5 LacO array in hypodermal cells of wildtype and unc-3 mutants show no statistically significant difference.
claims.source: If the change in compaction of the gcy-5 array were caused by unc-3 function, this change should be specific to neurons in which unc-3 acts as a terminal selector. Indeed, the size of the gcy-5 LacO array in hypodermal cells of wildtype and unc-3 mutants show no statistically significant difference (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: Loss of mes-2 permits CHE-1hs to induce gcy-5prom::gfp to the same extent as removal of unc-3 does.
claims.source: We found that loss of mes-2 permits CHE-1hs to induce gcy-5prom::gfp to the same extent as removal of unc-3 does (Figure 6A), indicating that mes-2 is indeed required for restriction of plasticity in cholinergic MNs.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Removal of both unc-3 and mes-2 leads to the induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in twice as many cells as seen in unc-3 or mes-2 mutants alone.
claims.source: To determine whether mes-2 acts in parallel or in the same pathway as unc-3, we tested mes-2; unc-3 double mutants and found that they have an additive phenotype. Removal of both unc-3 and mes-2 leads to the induction of gcy-5prom::gfp in twice as many cells as seen in unc-3 or mes-2 mutants alone.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: unc-3 and mes-2 work in parallel genetic pathways to ensure plasticity restriction in differentiated cholinergic MNs.
claims.source: This suggests that unc-3 and mes-2 work in parallel genetic pathways to ensure plasticity restriction in differentiated cholinergic MNs.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the additive phenotype of mes-2; unc-3 double mutants.

claims.claim: Both met-2 and set-25 mutants have significantly more gcy-5prom::gfp expressing cholinergic MNs compared to wildtype.
claims.source: Both met-2 and set-25 mutants have significantly more gcy-5prom::gfp expressing cholinergic MNs compared to wildtype.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: For set-25 the increase in gcy-5prom::gfp expression is only modest, and a met-2 set-25 double mutant is not significantly different from met-2.
claims.source: However, for set-25 the increase is only modest, and a met-2 set-25 double mutant is not significantly different from met-2, suggesting met-2, has a greater role in making the gcy-5prom::gfp locus inaccessible to CHE-1.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: An additive phenotype is not evident in met-2; unc-3, set-25; unc-3, or met-2 set-25; unc-3, suggesting that these factors might act in the same pathway to restrict the accessibility of gcy-5prom::gfp.
claims.source: An additive phenotype is not evident in met-2; unc-3, set-25; unc-3, or met-2 set-25; unc-3, suggesting that these factors might act in the same pathway to restrict the accessibility of gcy-5prom::gfp.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: met-2; set-25 double mutants lack H3K9me3 at the L4 and adult stages.
claims.source: Using antibody staining, we ensured that met-2; set-25 double mutants also lack H3K9me3 at the L4 and adult stages where we perform our experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Induction of CHE-1hs leads to increased activation of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs of met-2 single mutants and met-2 set-25 double mutants, but not in set-25 single mutants.
claims.source: We found that induction of CHE-1hs does lead to increased activation of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs of met-2 single mutants and met-2 set-25 double mutants, but not in set-25 single mutants (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: H3K9me1/2 and H3K9me3 have to be perturbed for CHE-1hs to activate gcy-5prom::gfp.
claims.source: This suggests that H3K9me1/2 and H3K9me3 have to be perturbed for CHE-1hs to activate gcy-5prom::gfp.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the met-2 and set-25 mutant data.

claims.claim: The loss of met-2; set-25 in transgenic worms containing the single copy hs::che-1 transgene results in the expression of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs.
claims.source: To ensure that our phenotype is not an artifact of repetitive transgenes, we confirmed that the loss of met-2; set-25 in transgenic worms containing the single copy hs::che-1 transgene also results in the expression of gcy-5prom::gfp in the cholinergic MNs and that the expression of gfp in these worms overlaps with gcy-5 mRNA expression as determined by smFISH of endogenous gcy-5 transcripts (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: None of the met-2;unc-3, set-25;unc-3 and met-2 set-25;unc-3 double and triple mutants show an additive effect that is significantly different from the phenotype of unc-3 single mutants.
claims.source: None of these double and triple mutants show an additive effect that is significantly different from the phenotype of unc-3 single mutants (Figure 6B), indicating that met-2, set-25, and unc-3 act in the same pathway rather than in parallel pathways.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: met-2, set-25, and unc-3 act in the same pathway rather than in parallel pathways.

results.result: Ectopic CHE-1 expression activates ASE-specific effector genes broadly in undifferentiated cells during early embryonic and larval development, but this activation becomes progressively restricted as cells differentiate, with differentiated cells becoming largely refractory to CHE-1 activity by the L4/adult stages.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C3, and C25-C44 provide comprehensive experimental evidence from multiple reporters (gcy-5prom::gfp, gcy-5fosmid::gfp, gcy-6, gcy-7), developmental stages, and tissue-specific promoters showing that CHE-1 can activate target genes in undifferentiated/differentiating cells but not in fully differentiated cells. The data include quantification across developmental stages, validation with endogenous mRNA (smFISH), and demonstration that CHE-1 protein is present and functional in all cell types (C34, C35). This represents a core finding of the manuscript.

results.result: Removal of terminal selectors (unc-3, ets-5, ttx-1, ceh-14, lin-11) in differentiated neurons enables ectopically expressed CHE-1 to activate ASE-specific effector genes, demonstrating that terminal selectors control restriction of cellular plasticity. However, not all terminal selectors (unc-30, unc-42) show this phenotype, and disruption of identity-specific transcriptional programs alone (unc-4, unc-55; mab-9) does not increase plasticity.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C5 and C45-C68 provide extensive experimental evidence across multiple terminal selector mutants showing increased CHE-1 responsiveness in 5 of 7 tested terminal selectors. The data include quantification, multiple markers, appropriate controls (C50, C55, C62-C65), and demonstrate that ~30% of affected neurons respond (C52, C57, C58, C61). The negative results with unc-30 and unc-42 (C62-C67) and with unc-4 and unc-55; mab-9 (C55-C56) strengthen the conclusion that terminal selectors have a specific plasticity-restricting function distinct from identity specification (C68). This is a major finding of the manuscript.

results.result: A hypomorphic unc-3::mNG::AID allele that allows near-normal cholinergic motor neuron differentiation and locomotion still retains plasticity in response to ectopic CHE-1, demonstrating that terminal selectors control restriction independently of specification.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C73 describe a critical genetic separation-of-function experiment. The unc-3::mNG::AID allele shows wildtype locomotion and near-wildtype expression of cholinergic markers (C69), yet displays the same plasticity phenotype as the unc-3 null allele (C70-C71). This provides strong evidence that the identity-specifying and plasticity-restricting functions of terminal selectors can be genetically separated (C73), supporting a key conceptual advance of the manuscript.

results.result: The chromatin structure of the CHE-1 target locus gcy-5 is less compact in unc-3 mutant cholinergic motor neurons compared to wildtype, as measured by LacO/LacI spot assay, suggesting that terminal selectors restrict plasticity by organizing chromatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C7 and C74-C78 provide direct evidence for chromatin compaction changes using the LacO/LacI spot assay. The ace-2 control locus shows expected compaction changes correlating with transcriptional activity (C74-C75), validating the assay. The gcy-5 locus shows increased spot size in unc-3 mutants (C76-C77), and this change is specific to neurons where unc-3 acts (C78). While the authors acknowledge the gcy-5 change is less dramatic than ace-2 (C77), the data support the conclusion that terminal selectors influence chromatin compaction.

results.result: H3K9 methyltransferases (met-2, set-25) and H3K27 methyltransferase (mes-2) contribute to restriction of plasticity in differentiated neurons. Genetic epistasis experiments suggest that H3K9 methylation acts in the same pathway as unc-3, while H3K27 methylation acts in parallel.
results.evaluation: Claims C8 and C79-C97 provide comprehensive genetic epistasis data showing that mes-2 mutants have increased plasticity and show an additive phenotype with unc-3 (C79-C81), while met-2 set-25 double mutants show increased plasticity but do not enhance the unc-3 phenotype (C82-C90). HP1 homologs (hpl-1, hpl-2) also contribute to restriction and show partial additivity with unc-3 (C92-C94). The data include appropriate controls (C85, C88, C95) and validation with single-copy transgenes and smFISH (C88). The epistasis analysis supports the model that H3K9me acts downstream of unc-3 while H3K27me acts in parallel (C97).

results.result: Terminal selectors coordinate identity specification with restriction of cellular plasticity by activating identity-specific genes while making non-identity-defining genes less accessible, serving as a checkpoint during differentiation. This is proposed to occur through a surveillance mechanism involving chromatin organization.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C10 and C98-C121 represent the main conceptual conclusions of the manuscript, synthesizing all experimental findings. The claims that terminal selectors coordinate specification with restriction (C10, C105, C121) and that terminal selector mutant neurons retain plasticity without being in a progenitor-like state (C98, C104) are well-supported by the experimental data. The proposed surveillance mechanism (C116-C117, C119-C121) is a reasonable model based on the genetic epistasis data, though the authors appropriately acknowledge uncertainty about the precise molecular mechanism. These conclusions represent the major conceptual advance of the work.

results.result: Background and context claims about terminal selectors, cellular plasticity, chromatin modifications, and prior work on developmental restriction are established through citations to the literature.
results.evaluation: Claims C1 and C11-C24, C39, C99-C102, C106 provide essential background context and are supported by appropriate citations to the literature. These claims establish the conceptual framework for the study and accurately represent prior work on terminal selectors, nuclear transplantation experiments, transcription factor overexpression studies, chromatin modifications, and developmental plasticity. The citations appear appropriate and the claims are consistent with established knowledge in the field.

results.result: In terminal selector mutants, only about 30% of affected neurons activate ASE-identity genes in response to CHE-1, and specific neurons (RIS, CEP, ASK, ASI) remain responsive to CHE-1 in wildtype adults, suggesting that restriction requires input from terminal selector-independent factors.
results.evaluation: Claims C32, C107-C108 describe the incomplete penetrance of the plasticity phenotype. The observation that only ~30% of neurons respond in terminal selector mutants (C107) is consistently reported across multiple mutants (C52, C57, C58, C61). The identification of specific neurons that remain CHE-1-responsive in wildtype adults (C32) is a direct observation. The conclusion that terminal selector-independent factors contribute to restriction (C108) is a reasonable inference from the incomplete penetrance, though the nature of these factors remains unknown.

results.result: Overall H3K9me3 levels appear unchanged in unc-3 mutants, and unc-3 does not regulate expression of met-2 or hpl-1/2 genes or act through positive histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K36me3), suggesting that unc-3 may regulate the distribution rather than the levels of H3K9me3.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C115 describe negative results and observations that help constrain the mechanism. The observation that overall H3K9me3 levels are unchanged in unc-3 mutants (C113) and that unc-3 does not regulate expression of chromatin modifiers (C114) or act through positive marks (C115) are supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The inference that unc-3 may regulate H3K9me3 distribution is reasonable but remains speculative as the authors acknowledge they could not test this directly. These are important mechanistic constraints but represent negative/inconclusive results.

results.result: One possible model is that terminal selectors directly activate target genes while also directly silencing non-expressed genes, but the authors disfavor this model due to the complexity it would require.
results.evaluation: Claim C118 describes a hypothetical model that the authors explicitly disfavor. This is presented as speculation and is not supported by experimental evidence. The authors argue against this model based on logical considerations about regulatory complexity, but no experiments directly test this possibility. This represents a discussion point rather than a supported result.
